prompt:
Sprite sheet for a 2D side-view narrative game: ten small figures of the same character, drawn as copper-plate engravings for a 19th-century book, each figure only about 200 pixels tall. The first reference image gives the exact layout, the exact size and the exact poses: ten figures in two rows of five, all at the same small scale, the feet of each row on the same baseline. Figures one to eight (in reading order) are a walk cycle to the right in strict side view; figure nine stands still in side view, both feet flat on the ground; figure ten has turned three-quarters towards the viewer. Copy every pose, the positions of both legs and feet, the arms, the parcel and the satchel, and the place and size of each figure exactly from the first reference; only the drawing changes. The first reference is a plain 3D render: take only the layout, the size and the poses from it, never its smooth shading or its plastic 3D look. The second reference image only shows the costume and the proportions of the character: do not copy its drawing style, its colours or its three-view layout. The third reference image shows the engraving technique and, most important, the line spacing and line width of the game at the size it is shown on screen: use exactly the same absolute spacing and width of the lines as in the third reference, so the small figures have fewer lines, not finer lines. The fourth reference image shows this character already drawn as an engraving at a larger size: keep its drawing, its face and its tone values, but draw it small with the coarser lines of the third reference; do not copy its layout or its size.

Technique: a copper-plate engraving with etching, printed in a single pure black ink on pure white paper (no tinted ground). Everything is built only from engraved lines: long parallel hatching, cross-hatching in two or three directions for the darks, swelling lines that are thick in the shadows and taper to hair-thin points in the light, short flicks and stipple dots for stone and rock, contour lines that follow the forms. The tone values come only from the thickness and spacing of the lines: no grey wash, no aquatint, no tonal gradients, no airbrush, no smudged pencil shading, no colour; between the lines the paper stays white. A firm, clear contour line around the figure and around every costume part; the hatching curves around the round body, the arms, the legs and the cap. Light from the upper left. The colours of the costume become tone values: the dark fur and the dark face stripes in dense, bold cross-hatching, the white face stripes and the light belly bare white paper inside a contour line, the cream shirt white with a few lines in the shadow, the dark green cap and vest in medium-dark hatching, the red scarf in medium hatching, the satchel dark, the parcel white with its string. Keep the face readable at this small size: a small black eye, a black nose, the broad white stripe of the face clearly separated from the dark stripe. Bold, open, clearly separated lines with white paper between them, never a grey mush and never fine hair lines. Not a cartoon, not a comic, not a 3D render, not a painting, not a pencil sketch, no colour.

The badger courier: an original mascot character, a stout, short-legged badger with a broad black-and-white striped face, wearing a dark green peaked cap with a brass button, a dark green vest with pockets over a cream shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a long red knitted scarf, a brown leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and a brown paper parcel tied with string under one arm.

Each figure isolated on a fully transparent background; inside the figure the white paper between the lines is opaque white. Clear empty space between the figures; no ground, no cast shadow, no frame borders, nothing cut off at the edge of the sheet.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.
